rounds.fact: MSN launched alongside Windows 95 as Microsoft's answer to AOL, bundling a dial-up service with a portal homepage that shipped as the default for millions of new PCs.
Technorati was built specifically to search and rank blogs during the mid-2000s blogging boom, back when blogs were treated as a distinct category from the rest of the web.
Bebo was massively popular in the UK and Ireland during the mid-2000s, at one point ranking as the third-most-visited social network in the US before AOL bought it for $850 million in 2008.

Slashdot popularized threaded, community-moderated comment sections years before that became standard, and getting linked from its front page could crash smaller sites entirely - a phenomenon known as 'the Slashdot effect.'
Woot's entire business model was selling exactly one product per day until it sold out, a simple gimmick that built a cult following before Amazon eventually bought the company.
